title: Fusion Add-in GitHub Tracker
summary: Builds a tracker dashboard for taking one Autodesk Fusion add-in to a public GitHub repo, from just its name: moving an existing add-in, or starting a new one in its repo.
what_it_is: A Claude skill that builds a **tracker dashboard**: a vibe-dashboard page with its own owner-only database, for one Fusion add-in on its way to a public GitHub repository. It follows the shape of the Selection Inspector move tracker (**Tue Nov 24, 2026**).

It has two paths. **Move** is for an add-in that already exists: Swami uploads its zip, and the steps run Instructions, Tracker, Audit, Create repo, First release, Future releases and Field guide. **New** is for an add-in built in its repo from day one: Instructions, Tracker, Create repo, Build on branch `dev`, First release, Future releases and Field guide.
Every step has a copyable prompt, a status and a done tick saved in the page's database, so any later chat can tick a step for Swami and the page stays the one record of where the job stands.
why: Moving the Selection Inspector add-in to GitHub taught lessons worth keeping, such as shipping the update check in the very first release. This skill bakes them into a tracker Claude builds fresh for each add-in, instead of re-planning every move from scratch.

what_it_does.text: Works out the path (an uploaded zip means move), the display and internal names, the repo name (`fusion-addin-<name>` under `swami-claude-skills`), a one-sentence description, the button location and, for a move, the uploaded version. It asks only for what it can't work out.

Gets the tracker kit from Swami's private repo `swami-claude-skills/vibe-dashboards`, folder `addin-tracker/`: `build_tracker.py`, `tracker.js`, `extra.css`, `post.py`, three patch files and two sample configs.
Writes a small `cfg.json` for the add-in, such as name, internal name, description, location, start date and path.
Builds the page with `build_tracker.py`, then runs vibe-dashboard's table-fit, toolbar, Search, Mind Map, source colour and tooltip patches in a fixed order.

The step table with a prompt per step, a diagram of the whole job with a colour key, Decisions, Links that turn live, the model and planned repo layouts as collapsible trees, a 15-check Test in Fusion list and Troubleshooting.

Looks at the diagram for overlaps and opens the page at 1440, 1000 and 390 px: no console errors, no sideways scroll on a phone, no system tooltips, every glossary term found, and 13 sections in order.
Records the audio overview from the narration draft the build writes, after the noun/verb stress audit.
Scans the page, narration and config against the project's own exclusion list before publishing; any real hit stops the publish.
Publishes the page with an owner-only database (steps, tests and links), checks the database, ticks step 2 done, and records the tracker link in project memory.

triggers: "Make a GitHub tracker for my Hole Counter add-in"
"I want to move Selection Inspector to GitHub" (with the add-in's zip)
"Start a new Fusion add-in in its own repo and give me a tracker"

how_to_use.step: In the Claude project for the add-in, ask for a tracker. For a move, upload the add-in's zip.
Answer any questions about the name, description or button location that Claude can't work out.
Claude gets the kit, builds and checks the page, records the audio, runs the privacy scan and publishes the tracker.
Add the tracker link to the project instructions, so every chat in the project ticks its steps there.
Copy each step's prompt into a chat. When a step is done, tick it on the page or ask Claude to tick it.
Run the Test in Fusion checks on your own computer; checks 13 to 15 need the second release.

how_to_use_windows.step: Building the tracker happens in Claude's workspace and on claude.ai, so these steps are the same on Windows 10 or 11.
The Test in Fusion checks run in Fusion on the Windows PC; where a step says Finder or Terminal, use File Explorer or PowerShell.

capabilities.text: Starts from just the add-in's name and works out the rest, asking only for what it can't.
Covers both a move of an existing add-in and a new add-in built in its repo from day one.
Ticks and statuses live in the page's own database, so they survive rebuilds and any chat can update them.
Bakes in what earlier moves taught: the update check ships in the first release, update-banner tests wait for the second, and the Claude GitHub app may need the new repo added.

limitations.text: It builds the tracker; the move or build itself happens later, step by step, from the prompts on the page.
The kit lives in Swami's private repo, so the skill only works on an account whose Claude GitHub app can reach that repo.
Only Swami, or Claude writing as him, can change a step's status or tick; other viewers see them read only.
Claude can't run the add-in in Fusion; the Test in Fusion checks are for Swami.

scheduled_tasks.summary: None. It runs when Swami asks for a tracker, and steps are ticked from chats. The nightly GitHub backup of Swami's artifacts also saves each tracker page, but that task is not part of this skill.

other_ais.notes: Skills need a Business, Enterprise, Edu or Healthcare plan. It has no claude.ai artifacts or artifact database, and no access to the private kit repo, so the tracker can't be built as designed.
Upload the unzipped skill folder. Same limits: no artifact database and no access to the private kit.
Import the .zip, or the SKILL.md if refused; installing by chat drifts. Same limits as the others.

gotchas.text: The first public release always includes the update check; a move's first release is a minor bump over the uploaded version, with no separate as-is release.
Update-banner checks 13 to 15 only work from the second release.
Add the new repo to the Claude GitHub app before the first push (github.com/settings/installations › Claude › Repository access; GitHub confirms by email).
Main gets no `version.json` until the first release, so the release workflow has nothing to publish while the add-in is built on `dev`.
Later republishes leave the capabilities out, so the database rules and saved ticks stay. Read a database doc before changing it, since writing it replaces the whole doc.
Never write the exclusion terms anywhere; refer to an exclusion only as "1 item excluded for privacy".

requirements.text: A Claude project for the add-in, with instructions that include its privacy exclusion list; the skill follows those instructions on top of its own.
Swami's GitHub connected to Claude, with the private vibe-dashboards repo reachable by the Claude GitHub app.
Code execution with network access, for the kit, the patches, the browser checks and the audio.
Nothing extra to build a tracker: works the same from Windows 10 or 11.

glossary.def: The vibe-dashboard page this skill builds: steps, prompts, ticks, diagram, links and checks for one add-in's trip to GitHub.
A Python program that adds commands or panels to Autodesk Fusion, installed in Fusion's AddIns folder.
The path for an add-in that already exists: it is audited, then published from a new repo.
The path for an add-in built in its repo from day one, on branch dev, until the first release.
A GitHub project folder with its full history. Each add-in gets its own public one.
A published version of the add-in on GitHub, with its zip, that users download and the update check looks for.
Code in the add-in that looks for a newer release and shows a banner, so users hear about fixes.
A separate line of work in a repo. The new path builds on dev and merges to main for the first release.
The scripts and files in Swami's private repo that build every tracker page.
The page's own owner-only store of step statuses, test ticks and live links, kept across republishes.
The tracker's list of 15 checks Swami runs in Fusion on a release.
The GitHub app that lets Claude read and push to Swami's repos; each repo must be added to it.
A check of the page, narration and config against the project's exclusion list before anything is published.
The spoken summary of the page, recorded by the vibe-dashboard skill and played under its title.
The copyable text for each step, pasted into a chat to have Claude do that step.

spoken.What It Is: It has two paths: move, for an add-in that already exists, and new, for one built in its repo from day one. Every step has a copyable prompt and a done tick saved in the page's own database

spoken.How to Use It: Ask for a tracker in the add-in's Claude project, answer any questions, add the tracker link to the project instructions, then work through the steps and tick each one when it's done

flow.alt: Workflow diagram: 1 Swami asks for a tracker in the add-in's Claude project, uploading the add-in's zip for a move, 2 Claude works out the path, names, repo name, description and button location, asking only for what it can't work out, 3 gets the tracker kit from Swami's private repo, 4 builds the page with vibe-dashboard's patches, 5 checks the page and records the audio, 6 runs the privacy scan, 7 publishes the tracker with its owner-only database, 8 Swami adds the tracker link to the project instructions, 9 works each step from its prompt and ticks it done, 10 runs the Test in Fusion checks on his computer.
flow.caption: Read left to right along the top row, right to left along the middle row, then left to right along the bottom. Swami asks, links the tracker, works its steps and tests; Claude builds and publishes it.
